proposals.relationship: Uses Ricœur’s account of memory, historical explanation and narrative to articulate the historian’s work and its civic responsibilities.
proposals.evidence_note: Own2011 answer finds Ricœur’s three event strata operational; own2017 positive exposition76–79 supports the particular resource. Own2012 retrospective discovery of agreement during Structuralism research precedes biography and later personal contact; friendship or biography alone is not treated as influence. Full original works unread.
primary_locators: 2012 answer beginning It is a virus and following answers

proposals.relationship: Recalls reading and commenting on chapters of Memory, History, Forgetting and guiding Ricœur through historiographical work, especially Certeau.
proposals.evidence_note: Dosse’s own2012 retrospective testimony, not an independently inspected manuscript. His account says the intellectual biography preceded their meetings and that Ricœur then sent chapters for corrections. Intended preface to the collective Certeau volume was not completed for health reasons; do not assert it appeared.
primary_locators: 2012 exchange following MM: A fantastic position! and preceding chapter-sending paragraph

proposals.relationship: Argues that Ricœur’s discussion misses Nora’s particular problem of lieux de mémoire despite their close methodological possibilities.
proposals.evidence_note: Own2011 qualified objection to this specific reading in Memory, History, Forgetting, alongside substantial agreement with Ricœur. Does not make hostility or reject his philosophy wholesale. The original exchange in Le Débat and complete books unread.

proposals.relationship: Uses Certeau’s historiographical operation and attention to singular cases and the historian’s position to develop a reflexive history.
proposals.evidence_note: Own2011 answer explicitly values marginal cases and own2012 attributes reflexive inscription to Certeau.2017 Certeau passages partly explain Ricœur’s use rather than a separate firsthand encounter. Dosse explicitly says he never met Certeau; no personal mentorship inferred.
primary_locators: 2012 answers on IHTP and biography distance

proposals.relationship: Uses Nora’s lieux de mémoire to treat changing traces and appropriations of the past as objects of historical inquiry.
proposals.evidence_note: Own2011 discussion identifies a methodological opening across periods, reinforced in2012 and2017 conclusion. This is specific analytical use, not a resource inferred merely because Dosse wrote Nora’s biography. The complete original collective work unread. Own2012 additionally recalls Nora supplying crucial details during biographical research under an agreement to maintain distance; this bounded informant contribution is consolidated here, not a claim Nora controlled or endorsed the finished book.
primary_locators: 2012 answer on Joan of Arc and present time
2012 answer beginning In relation to the biography of Paul Ricoeur, following empathy exchange

proposals.relationship: Uses Hartog’s regimes of historicity and presentism to diagnose an obscured future and the expansion of memorial demands.
proposals.evidence_note: Own2011 explicitly adopts Hartog’s hypothesis and own2017 attributes the conceptual diagnosis at68/72. No general pupil relation, no historical inevitability, and no current legal claim. Original Hartog books unread.

proposals.relationship: Uses Bloch’s distinction between historical inquiry and judicial sentencing to argue for understanding rather than verdicts.
proposals.evidence_note: Own2017 explicit deployment of Apologie at67/70 and1914 testimony speech at70. The latter is expressly cited through Olivier Dumoulin in note10, while note11 identifies the1974 Apologie edition. Underlying Bloch/Dumoulin texts unread; mediation retained.

proposals.relationship: Draws on Ginzburg’s evidentiary reasoning and Menocchio study to connect proof with singular cases that unsettle broad social categories.
proposals.evidence_note: Two particular uses: own2011 microhistory argument and own2017 judge/historian discussion. Dosse’s2011 apparent Friuli dating is not certified or propagated. Notes7–8 identify1980 Signes and1997 French Le juge et l’historien; originals unread, not collapsed into one book.

proposals.relationship: Invokes Febvre’s criticism of official national history and account of historical construction to defend critical inquiry.
proposals.evidence_note: Own2017 positive use67 and75. The article describes the inaugural occasion as1919, while note4 cites the1920 journal publication; both are kept distinct. A separate1932 lecture is mentioned at75. These originals unread; no claim that quoted formulas alone establish formal training.

proposals.relationship: Treats Le dimanche de Bouvines as a methodological opening toward the changing memorial traces of an event.
proposals.evidence_note: Own2011 paragraphs25/33 explicitly use Duby’s1973 study to shift attention toward subsequent traces and legitimize approaches beyond contemporary periods. Later Nora preface distinguished; complete book unread.

proposals.relationship: Uses Foucault’s Pierre Rivière case as an example of a singular history that exposes conflicts between medical and juridical authority.
proposals.evidence_note: Own2011 specific positive example within his argument for singular cases; co-workers in the collective Rivière publication are not erased or treated as Dosse’s teachers. Original collective case study unread. This does not rely on the problematic ancient-sexuality illustration at2017 p69.

proposals.relationship: Treats Corbin’s Pinagot study as an innovative limit experiment connecting an ordinary life with social history.
proposals.evidence_note: Own2011 favorable characterization within his account of why he wrote Le pari biographique. Resource describes this selected methodological use and does not rule out criticisms elsewhere. Pinagot book and complete Dosse book unread; loose interview language about absent archives is not certified as a literal no-evidence claim.

proposals.relationship: Rejects Braudel’s reported dismissal of events in favor of a history that takes actors and singular situations seriously.
proposals.evidence_note: Own2011 explicit disagreement in paragraph36, alongside his account of pragmatic/hermeneutic turns and rejection of simple relativism. Braudel’s phrase is reported by Dosse; original work and full Dosse2010 monograph unread. Existing Prost→Braudel edge1755 remains Prost’s own, Dosse-mediated argument.

proposals.relationship: Credits Halbwachs’s distinction between memory and history while arguing that distinction should permit their articulation.
proposals.evidence_note: Own2011 paragraph17 credits Cadres sociaux and Mémoire collective; follows it with a qualification against radical separation. This specific appropriation is not a formal genealogy or a statement of agreement with every consequence. Complete originals unread.

proposals.relationship: Questions a radical separation of memory and history in the implications he draws from Halbwachs’s account.
proposals.evidence_note: Own2011 qualified interpretation: Dosse says if one pushes Halbwachs’s thought to its ultimate consequences, history begins when memory ends. Preserve that modal attribution rather than present it as a direct absolute quotation or reject Halbwachs’s entire work.

proposals.relationship: Uses the Wilson biography attributed to Freud as a negative example of biographical hostility to its subject.
proposals.evidence_note: Own2012 brief but explicit methodological judgment, contrasting empathy with a biography he considers unsuccessful. The work is coauthored with William C. Bullitt, not Freud alone; bibliographic coauthor credit checked against Routledge publisher record, https://www.routledge.com/link/link/p/book/9781138540705 (copyright1966). No complete original or general rejection of psychoanalysis claimed.
primary_locators: 2012 answer to MM: I would like to make a provocation, beginning It is not necessarily easier

proposals.relationship: Invokes Lévi-Strauss’s bricolage as an analogy for the singular construction of Menocchio’s culture.
proposals.evidence_note: Own2011 paragraph34 describes Ginzburg’s Menocchio through this named conceptual analogy. This establishes the particular use, not direct reading of a specified Lévi-Strauss text or formal mentorship; complete original works unread. Claude Lévi-Strauss is distinct from Giovanni Levi.

proposals.relationship: Applies Freudian categories of repression, return and obsession to the changing forms of collective memory.
proposals.evidence_note: Own2011 paragraph22 explicitly endorses this conceptual use after discussing Rousso, Joutard and Stora as historical examples. These named mediations remain; no direct reading of a particular Freud text or general equation of individual and collective processes is certified. Coexists with his distinct negative2012 judgment of the Wilson biography.
